nodes.title: Is the router powered on?
nodes.body: Ask the customer to look at the power LED on the front panel.

nodes.title: Check the power supply
nodes.body: Confirm the adapter is seated at both the wall and the router.

snippets.label: Ticket note
snippets.text: Customer confirmed router had no power. Advised checking adapter at both ends.

nodes.title: What colour is the internet LED?
nodes.body: Green means sync. Red or off means no line. Amber means syncing.

attachments.caption: LED positions on the front panel

nodes.title: Reseat the WAN cable
nodes.body: Unplug and firmly reconnect the cable at the router and the wall socket.

snippets.label: Ticket note
snippets.text: Advised customer to reseat WAN cable at both ends. Awaiting result.

nodes.title: Wait two minutes for sync
nodes.body: Amber means the line is negotiating. This can take up to two minutes.

nodes.title: Power cycle the router
nodes.body: Unplug for 30 seconds, plug back in, wait for the router to fully boot.

nodes.title: Recheck the cable before escalating
nodes.body: A loose WAN cable is the most common cause of a failed power cycle.

nodes.title: Can the customer reach a website?
nodes.body: Have them open a browser and load any site over Wi-Fi.

nodes.title: Arrange a replacement power supply
nodes.body: Router hardware fault. Raise a hardware dispatch.

snippets.label: Ticket note
snippets.text: Router does not power on with known-good outlet. Dispatching replacement PSU.

nodes.title: Escalate to line diagnostics
nodes.body: Raise to tier 2 with the LED state and everything already attempted.

snippets.label: Escalation summary
snippets.text: Power confirmed. WAN cable reseated. Power cycle performed. No sync achieved. Escalating for line test.

nodes.title: Resolved
nodes.body: Confirm the customer is browsing normally, then close the ticket.

snippets.label: Closing note
snippets.text: Connectivity restored and confirmed by customer. Closing ticket.
